subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning to keep the vehicle model static without joints since it's just scenery, using the builder's part and shape primitives to construct it with a reasonably rich but low-risk structure.

I'm sketching out the chassis dimensions, roughly 9m long and 3m wide, with the lower hull box, upper deck, and wheel placement all mapped against ground level, plus outrigger pads for stability. I'm working through how to extrude the hull's side profile across the vehicle's width using the correct axis directions for the geometry.

Now I'm designing the front cab with a slanted windshield profile and a glowing cyan window effect, then moving on to laying out the six wheels along the z-axis.

Still building wheel geometry...

I'm trimming part counts down, then moving on to axles with a differential bulge, and now placing outrigger legs that extend sideways from the hull down to ground pads for stability.

Adding the diagonal brace rods and hex-sided pads, then moving to the railgun turret design—a lathe-built ring base with a tilted barrel mount angled 25° upward, computing the direction vector and local coordinate frame for placing the rail housings along the barrel length.

Still building the gun geometry...

Barrel extends past the cab fine with a support cradle added at front, and the gun clears the cab roof height-wise. Now I'm planning the detail pass: headlights, bumper, hazard stripe and emblem decals, antenna, exhaust stacks, roof lights, tow hooks, hatch, ladder, side vents, tool boxes, and a camouflage paint pattern across the hull.

Writing paint and geometry helpers...

Still building wheel geometry...

Switching to 12 treads so one lands at the bottom, keeping sink minimal. Now I'm adding mudguard arches above the wheels, dark inner arch panels, sloped fender plates, and mudflaps, plus axle cylinders and a sphere differential housing, before moving on to the leg structure function.

Adding the hexagonal base pad, ball joint sphere, and a support brace rod connecting the hull to the housing, deciding bones aren't strictly required for static models. I'm also adding a hazard warning plane on the outward face of the housing before moving on to the hull details.

Now I'm working through side panels, vents, tool boxes, and skirt lights, plus placing an "RG-6" decal plane on each hull side. I'm carefully working out the orientation math so the decal text reads correctly when viewed from either side, accounting for how the viewer's right-hand direction flips depending on which face they're looking from.

Moving to the top deck, I'm adding a hatch cylinder, roof lights, rod-and-sphere antennas, and a glowing rear capacitor bank, then starting to define the cab's extruded profile with a slanted windshield.

Computing cab geometry and windshield placement...

Simplifying the hull profile to avoid the cab-hood overlap, placing headlights at the front face, and adding bumper, tow hooks, and grille slat details. Planning panelled paint patches for the hull armor plating.

Settling on a color palette (olive, dark, steel, gunmetal, tire black, cyan, amber, red, hazard texture) and deciding rails get gunmetal paint with flat cyan glow strips. Now sketching out the SVG textures: hazard stripes, a window texture with blue gradient and cyan reflective streaks, and a number plate texture.

Designing the number plate "RG-6" with a star emblem, plus a circular crosshair/lightning emblem in red and white, hazard-striped warning panels, and box-based vent grilles. Setting window glow strength to 0.6, then adding rear details -- glowing tail lights, exhaust stack cylinders, a hazard rear plate, a hitch -- and horizontal cylindrical fuel tanks on the sides.

Checking for collisions between the side fuel tanks and the outrigger booms/legs, I'm deciding to skip the side tanks near the wheels since they overlap with the boom housings, and instead placing drum cylinders and an ammo crate on the deck behind the cab at x ±0.9.

Now I'm working out the turret geometry: positioning it at z -1.0 spanning roughly z -2.6 to 0.6, with the trunnion mount at y 3.3 above the turret top at 2.7. I'm defining the cradle side plates as extruded shapes at x ±0.85-0.95 connecting the turret to the pivot cylinder, and starting to size the gun breech width.

Continuing to place rear deck equipment like the capacitor bank, exhaust stacks, and turret details including the ring lathe outline and a hatch cylinder on the turret top.

For the turret's sloped front plate I'm thinking of using a chamfer-style rotated box rather than a full frustum shape. For elevation hydraulics, I'm adding rod segments connecting the turret pivot points down to the breech underside, using tapered thickness via interpolation for a sleeved look.

Now for the muzzle I'm placing a brake box with glowing side slits, then adding barrel rails spanning the full length with periodic coil rings (octagonal cylinders) along the barrel, plus thinner glowing accent rings at the front, and inner glow strips running between the rails.

I'm also adding small insulator spacer blocks between rails at regular intervals positioned lower in the bore, cooling fins near the breech, and setting flat shading on the cylinder rings to match the faceted box geometry.

Now I'm fleshing out exterior details: amber roof light bars on the cab, fender boxes over the wheel wells, and side door panels on the hull positioned to clear the wheels without overlapping.

I realize the outrigger booms at the sides would clash with the door panels, so I'm shifting the booms to z ±1.5 between the wheels and raising a decal strip above the fenders at y1.65 to hold the hazard striping and number markings, keeping everything clear of the wheels and fenders.

I'm now placing the fender boxes themselves—sized roughly 0.75×0.1×1.6 centered at x=±1.55, y=1.38—so they sit just above the wheel tread and line up with the hull wall, plus adding a vertical lip plate on the outer edge of each fender for detail.

Checking the boom position against the fender and wheel geometry, clearances look fine, so now I'm setting up the stabilizer legs at z=±1.5, deciding to keep them deployed with ground pads while the wheels also stay touching, then starting to write the actual build script importing the builder, SVG utilities, and the metal/panelled kit components.

Writing extrude and rail helper code...

I'll add a tilted whip antenna rod with a glowing red tip sphere, keeping the overall color palette limited so it stays manageable.
